first_impression.reaction: Googled 'corfu wedding venues' because Corfu's on our list and I'm comparing three planners. The intro gives me criteria (guest count, ceremony type, view) instead of 'paradise'. Went to the FAQ first, then the table, which reads like my own spreadsheet with the blanks admitted. Read the venues that could fit our numbers, the weather table and the legal bit properly. Mostly the numbers hold up when I cross-check them, but I caught the table rounding up one venue's view, and the 'your Advisor confirms it in writing' line comes round five times.

journey.quote: The right area depends on how many guests you are inviting, the kind of ceremony you want and the view you want behind you when you say your vows.
When you have a first shortlist, book a Wedded Concierge consultation and your Wedded Advisor will check those venues against your date and guest count.
journey.reaction: At least it says 'when you have a shortlist' rather than 'book now'. Still, it's a booking link before I've seen one venue. Minor.

journey.section: Corfu wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: It is not a ranking. "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail on its own site.
journey.reaction: Good. No fake 'number one', and the blanks are honest. That's why I trust the numbers that are filled in.

journey.quote: At Atlantica Grand Mediterraneo it means the resort hosts only one wedding on your chosen day, not that the resort closes to other guests.
journey.reaction: That's the catch I'd be looking for, and they've pointed it out themselves.

journey.quote: Atlantica asks couples marrying there to arrive at least three working days before the wedding and stay two working days after.
journey.reaction: A real constraint that costs guests annual leave. Nobody selling the venue leads with that.

journey.quote: Grecotel's wedding page lists Villa Medusa at the Kommeno peninsula as a luxury private villa: "your striking private traditional Corfiot Mansion in the Ionian countryside", offered for "intimate sumptuous celebrations with curated menu and set up".
journey.reaction: Countryside, then two lines later it's a beachfront villa with 'Direct Sea View' on a different page. Which is it? The table just says 'Direct sea view' as if it's settled. I'd want those two descriptions reconciled before I believed the view.

journey.quote: The two named capacities top out at 50, so for a larger guest list ask what Yali holds before you shortlist.
journey.reaction: Tells me where the page runs out instead of papering over it. Useful.

journey.quote: The fresco in the Nafsika Hall is by the artist Eirini Daniolou Neophytou.
journey.reaction: Two lines up it's the 'Nausica Ballroom'. Same room or a different one? Small, but I notice inconsistent names.

journey.quote: Its published terms are dated 2023, so ask for current terms.
journey.reaction: A date on the figures and a warning about their shelf life. That's the standard I want.

journey.quote: Outdoor receptions start from 20:30, and outdoor music stops at 23:30, after which the party can move indoors to the main restaurant until 04:00 at the latest. Fireworks are not allowed.
journey.reaction: Actual house rules with times. More useful than every 'breathtaking' on every other site combined.

journey.quote: Because the ceremony venues are listed as symbolic, a couple wanting a legally registered marriage should plan the civil step separately.
journey.reaction: Points out a limitation of a big-name resort. Good.

journey.quote: "360-degree views over the sparkling waters of the Ionian Sea to one side."
journey.reaction: 360 degrees, to one side? The line above says it looks inland to the mountain on the other side. So the sea is on one side. But the table says '360-degree views over the Ionian', which drops the 'one side' bit and overstates it. That's exactly the kind of rounding-up I check for, and now I'm rechecking the other table cells.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing for your date.
journey.reaction: Some version of this closes Kommeno, Corfu Town, Kalami, the south-east and the west. Once is a service. Five times sounds like a sales script, and it makes the blanks look like they're there to sell the Advisor.

journey.section: Getting to Corfu for your wedding
journey.quote: The airport sits close to most of this list.
journey.reaction: You give distances for two venues. Nothing for Kalami, Angsana or Courti. 'Most' isn't backed up by what's on the page.

journey.quote: September is a similar temperature, but rainfall climbs sharply, with an average of 87.8 mm against 21.7 mm in August.
journey.reaction: Named source, real numbers, and a trade-off I wouldn't have guessed. That's how you earn trust.

journey.quote: Wildfires occur during the extended summer from June to September, can start with little warning and travel quickly, so follow local authorities' advice.
journey.reaction: Most wedding sites would leave this out. Dated, sourced, not buried.

journey.quote: All notarial services need an appointment, though apostille and CNI documents can be sent by post. The Embassy gives no legal advice, and fees apply.
journey.reaction: Specific and linked to the Embassy. Says what they won't do, too.

journey.section: Shortlist your Corfu venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal. Still doesn't tell me how the fee's worked out, or whether any of these venues pay you as well.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these venues, and does that affect which ones the Wedded Advisor recommends?
How is the Wedded Concierge fee calculated and what does it cover?
Is the first consultation free, and what do I come away with?
Is the Villa Medusa on the wedding page the countryside mansion or the beachfront villa, and does it actually have the sea view?
How far are Kalami, Angsana and The Courti Estate from the airport?
Is there a real Corfu wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: | The Courti Estate | South-east coast | Private estate | 360-degree views over the Ionian |
turn_offs_found.why: The venue's own words, quoted further down, are sea views 'to one side', with the mountain inland on the other. The table cuts the qualifier and makes it sound like sea all round. If one cell is rounded up, I have to recheck all the others.

turn_offs_found.quote: The airport sits close to most of this list.
turn_offs_found.why: Only two venues get a distance or drive time. 'Most' is a claim the page doesn't back with numbers, and numbers are what I came for.

turn_offs_found.quote: When you have a first shortlist, book a Wedded Concierge consultation and your Wedded Advisor will check those venues against your date and guest count.
turn_offs_found.why: It comes after four bullet points and before the table or any venue. The wording is softer than usual, so it's minor, but the pitch still comes before the proof.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the comparison table and the exclusive-use explanation
My dad, the weather table with the September rainfall and the wildfire and CNI paragraphs

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, shortlist your Corfu venues with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: The page mostly earned it: dated terms, published house rules, honest blanks, downsides named, risks sourced. What holds me back: the table oversells The Courti Estate's view, so I'd recheck the other cells first. And I still don't know whether you take a cut from the venues. The fee-in-writing line helps, but it doesn't answer that.

top_3_changes: Fix The Courti Estate's table cell (must-fix): '360-degree views over the Ionian' overstates the venue's own wording ('to one side'). Make the table match the quote in the body. While there, reconcile Villa Medusa's 'Ionian countryside' description with the 'Direct sea view' table cell, and use one spelling for the Nausica/Nafsika room.
Cut the repeated 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing for your date' lines from five to one or two. Optionally move the first Concierge link below the comparison table.

Either back 'The airport sits close to most of this list' with distances for the other areas or soften it to the two venues you have figures for. (Commission and fee-model detail would also help, but that's a deferred business detail, so nice-to-have.)

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and table first, cross-checked figures against each other, looked for catches, fee model, commissions
No invented brand facts; fee, commission and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or 'how we know' lines

open_questions.question: The Courti Estate table cell ('360-degree views over the Ionian') vs the body quote ('to one side') is a factual consistency fix, not a business detail. Is the writer picking this up this round, along with the Villa Medusa countryside/sea-view wording and the Nausica/Nafsika spelling?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'corfu wedding venues' while comparing three planners; Corfu is a live option, hence high relevance.
No prices on the page is deliberate and not penalised.
Venue puffery inside quotation marks (e.g. 'Greece's most impressively located hotel') is clearly attributed to the venue, so it is not counted as the brand's own unsupported claim.
Title is person-set and deferred, so not flagged.
